facebook.long_form:
You cannot count out the Los Angeles Lakers.

Down 18 points and staring at a home loss, LA flipped the script and stormed back to force overtime. Then they did something even more impressive — they held the Charlotte Hornets completely scoreless for the final 4 minutes and 24 seconds of overtime. Final score: Lakers 118, Hornets 114.

It was a remarkable defensive stand that sealed one of the more stunning comeback wins you'll see this season. After trailing by double digits, the Lakers' defense suffocated Charlotte when it mattered most. No buckets for the Hornets down the stretch — just clock ticking away as the Lakers walked away with the W.

The Lakers aren't going away without a fight this season. When this team locks in defensively, they're dangerous.

The Utah Jazz may be one of the NBA's youngest and least-experienced rosters this season, but on Tuesday night they looked nothing like a team with a 2-13 record.

Utah walked into the Clippers' arena and put on a show, winning 132-107. The final score wasn't even close — this was a dominant performance from start to finish. The Jazz outscored Los Angeles by 25 points, playing with energy and confidence that completely caught the Clippers off guard.

For LA, it's a stinging loss that highlights the dangers of underestimating any team on any given night. The NBA is a brutal league, and nobody gets a free night. The Clippers will need to regroup quickly with more games on the horizon.

For Utah? This one goes in the memory bank as a reminder that the talent is there, even if the wins haven't come consistently.
